explanation: Aluminium doesn't react with cold or hot water, but reacts with steam to form aluminium oxide and hydrogen gas — the same pattern iron follows, just with a metal that only needs a thin oxide coating to show it.

beaker_view.initial_appearance: A grey aluminium strip, held in a stream of steam.
beaker_view.final_appearance: Coated with a dull grey-white oxide layer.

thermal.visual_cue: Needs a continuous stream of steam to react at all.

beaker_view.observation: Held in the steam, the aluminium slowly develops a dull oxide coating as hydrogen gas is given off.
